glossary.op_ct_utc: Coordinated Universal Time (UTC). Days are counted from the day of greatest eclipse; a cross-day contact is marked +1 or −1.
glossary.op_approx: c. = circa, approximately. No known observation site lies within 90 km, so this point is named by its nearest geographic region rather than by a place.
glossary.hora_mechanism: One of the twelve unequal hours: daylight (I–XII from sunrise) and night (from sunset) are each divided into twelve, stretching with the season. d. = diei (day), n. = noctis (night).

glossary.cal_julian: Julian calendar, in common use before the 1582 calendar reform; equivalent to Gregorian {date}
glossary.saros: Serial number of an eclipse within a saros series, successive eclipses about 18 years 11 days apart
glossary.obscuration: Fraction of the sun's area covered by the Moon, distinct from magnitude measured by diameter
glossary.gamma: Least distance of the shadow axis from Earth's centre in Earth radii; smaller absolute values are more central
glossary.ecl_magnitude: Fraction of the sun's or moon's diameter covered at greatest eclipse
glossary.status_predicted_unseen: Predicted, not observed — the eclipse did occur astronomically, but at greatest eclipse the eclipsed body lay below the local horizon or the local magnitude was near zero, so it could not be seen here; this locality was assigned by computational matching, not by eyewitness record
glossary.status_predicted_nonevent: Predicted, did not occur — the source expected an eclipse on this date from calendrical prediction, but recomputation shows none was visible here; it records a forecast eclipse that failed to appear, flagged to distinguish it from an eyewitness sighting
glossary.status_obscured: Clouded out — the eclipse was geometrically visible from this place, but the source itself records that cloud hid it. The obstruction was weather, not geometry: an eclipse did occur here, and the record shows observers watching for it
glossary.ecl_ecliptic: The track the centre of Earth's shadow traces: the ecliptic
glossary.ecl_moonpath: The track the Moon traces through Earth's shadow: the lunar path; the arrow marks its direction of motion
glossary.ecl_sunpath: The Sun's apparent path across the sky; the arrow marks its direction of motion
glossary.ecl_c_greatest: Greatest eclipse, the instant of maximum coverage
glossary.ecl_c_greatest_geo_solar: The instant the shadow axis passes closest to Earth's centre, and where that axis meets the surface
glossary.ecl_c_greatest_geo_lunar: The instant the Moon's centre passes closest to Earth's shadow axis, and the sublunar point at that moment
glossary.ecl_c_p1_solar: First contact, the Moon's disc first touches the Sun and the partial phase begins
glossary.ecl_c_p2_solar: Second contact: the Moon fully covers the Sun and totality or annularity begins
glossary.ecl_c_p3_solar: Third contact: the Sun begins to reappear and totality or annularity ends
glossary.ecl_c_p4_solar: Last contact, the Moon's disc leaves the Sun and the eclipse ends
glossary.ecl_c_sunrise: The Sun rises already eclipsed, the first contact having passed before sunrise
glossary.ecl_c_sunset: The Sun sets while still eclipsed, the last contact falling after sunset
glossary.ecl_c_moonrise: The Moon rises already eclipsed, the earlier contacts lay below the horizon before moonrise
glossary.ecl_c_moonset: The Moon sets while still eclipsed, the later contacts lie below the horizon and are not visible from here
glossary.ecl_c_p1_lunar: The Moon enters Earth's penumbra, its disc dimming slightly
glossary.ecl_c_u1: The Moon's edge enters Earth's umbra and the partial phase begins
glossary.ecl_c_u2: The Moon is fully inside the umbra and totality begins
glossary.ecl_c_u3: Third contact: the Moon's edge leaves Earth's umbra and totality ends
glossary.ecl_c_u4: The Moon fully leaves the umbra and the partial phase ends
glossary.ecl_c_p4_lunar: The Moon leaves Earth's penumbra, its disc restored to full brightness
glossary.ecl_par: Duration of the partial phase of a lunar eclipse
glossary.ecl_total: Duration of the total phase of a lunar eclipse
glossary.ecl_gamma: Least distance of the Moon's centre from the shadow axis in Earth radii, positive when north of the axis
glossary.ecl_umag: Umbral magnitude, the fraction of the Moon's diameter covered by the umbra at greatest eclipse
glossary.duration_total: Length of time an observer experiences a total solar or lunar eclipse
glossary.duration_partial: Length of time the sun's or moon's disc is partly covered
glossary.duration_penumbral: Length of time the moon lies within Earth's penumbra
